args: Analyze the failure-path pointer synchronization bug in `xmlLoadEntityContent` in `libxml2/parser.c` around line 8200. What is the safest minimal root-cause fix when `xmlParserInputBufferGrow` reallocates `input->buf->buffer`, and a later grow fails leaving `buf->error` set so `xmlBufResetInput` refuses to refresh `input->base/cur/end`? Consider whether synchronization should happen after every successful grow, whether offsets must be preserved, and whether changing `xmlBufResetInput` globally would be unsafe.

The provided ASan report shows a heap-use-after-free during error reporting: `xmlLoadEntityContent` repeatedly grows an external entity input buffer; an earlier successful realloc frees the allocation cached by active `xmlParserInput` pointers, then a later allocation-injected grow failure sets the xmlBuf error. The function calls `xmlBufResetInput`, but that helper returns early when the buffer has an error, then calls `xmlFatalErr`, whose context printer reads stale `input->cur`. I am inspecting `libxml2/parser.c`, `libxml2/buf.c`, and `libxml2/xmlIO.c`. No patch has been made yet. The likely strategy is to refresh parser input pointers immediately after each successful growth, before any later operation can fail, while preserving the intended offset semantics.
